intended_object: The identity comparison between the carrier of the bundled finite-projective product module `FiniteProjective.prodRight R S M N` and the underlying `ModuleCat.prodRight R S M.obj N.obj`. The docstring itself says it is "the identity on pairs".
explanation: The body is `LinearEquiv.refl` on `ModuleCat.prodRight R S M.obj N.obj`. Both sides are definitionally the same type: `FiniteProjective.prodRight` is the full-subcategory object whose `obj` is `ModuleCat.prodRight R S M.obj N.obj`. So this is only a bookkeeping device that moves between the bundled finite-projective object and its underlying module category object. It is an internal transport and has no standalone mathematical meaning. Mathematically it is just the identity map on M × N. It is correct as stated, but it is not a mathematical object to be judged for faithfulness.
